messages.subject: MGCFA continuous or categorical?
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I'm new in the group and have a question.
Does the multiple-group CFA conducted by mirt treat items as "continuous" or "categorical"?
Is there a way to shift between the two modes? 
Best
Maya

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: MGCFA continuous or categorical?
parts:
The public versions of mirt treat all response observations as categorical. There has been a small amount of work on the dev version to include continuous IRT models, but I haven't followed up on this as the applications seem quite limited (aside from, perhaps, beta unfolding response models and friends). 

Phil

On Wed, Oct 9, 2024 at 3:29 PM Maya Rohimah Atmawinata <mayarohima...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello Phil,

Thanks for your prompt response. The name of the package ‘mirt’ implies that it estimates only IRT models, but it seems that one can also use it for CFA.

It's somewhat semantics. IRT is factor analysis of categorical data, where classical versions of IRT are basically some version of one factor models with various response functions. Sometimes the FA models with special link functions will match the response models found in IRT, such as the 2PL and GRM.

Are the CFA models (single group & multiple group) estimated by mirt the same or comparable to those estimated by Mplus or lavaan? What can I do to make the mirt output as similar to Mplus output as possible? I mean the choice of the estimation method, etc.

If you use the weighted likelihood estimators in lavaan/Mplus for categorical response variables you'll obtain limited information estimates of specific types of IRT models that assume ordinal responses. Might be worthwhile to read an article or two on this, such as the following:

Wirth, R. & Edwards, M. C.
Item factor analysis: Current approaches and future directions.
Psychological Methods, American Psychological Association, 2007, 12, 58-79

Best regards

Maya
